summary: When a field made hekdesh is sold, the owner is asked to offer a price first, because he adds a fifth. A story of a man who offered almost nothing for his poor field.

chunks.he: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֶת שָׂדֵהוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ יוֹבֵל,
chunks.en: Someone who makes his field hekdesh at a time when Yovel is not kept,
chunks.st: In the case of one who consecrates his ancestral field during a period when the Jubilee Year is not observed,
chunks.stMore: and therefore the field is not redeemed according to a fixed rate of fifty shekels per beit kor but according to its value,

chunks.en: they say to him, "You start first,"

chunks.stMore: how much do you offer for its redemption?

chunks.en: because the owner adds a fifth,
chunks.st: This method is advantageous for the Temple treasury, as the owner gives an additional payment of one-fifth of the value of the field,

chunks.en: and any other person does not add a fifth.
chunks.st: and every other person does not give an additional one-fifth payment.

summary: When another person offers more than the owner, how much must the owner pay to keep his field? He adds a fifth only to his own offer.

chunks.en: If the owner offered twenty, and another person said,
chunks.st: If the owner says he will pay twenty sela and one other person said:

chunks.en: "It is mine for twenty-one,"
chunks.st: The field is hereby mine for a payment of twenty-one sela,

chunks.en: the owner gives twenty-six.
chunks.explain: His twenty, plus a fifth, plus one more sela.
chunks.st: the owner gives twenty-six sela and takes the field.
chunks.stMore: He pays the twenty that he initially offered; plus five sela, which is one-fifth of the total future sum, i.e., one-quarter of his initial offer. In addition, he adds one sela, the difference between his initial offer and that of the other person, so that the Temple treasury will not receive less than the twenty-one sela offer proposed by the other person.

summary: A person may give some of his things as cherem, but not all of them.

chunks.en: A person may give as cherem some of his sheep and cattle,
chunks.explain: Cherem is something given as holy, usually to the Kohanim.
chunks.st: A person may dedicate, for sacred or priestly use, some of his flock and some of his cattle,

chunks.en: of his Canaanite slaves and maidservants,
chunks.st: and some of his Canaanite slaves and maidservants,

chunks.st: But if he dedicated all that he has of any type of property,

chunks.en: they are not cherem,
chunks.st: they are not dedicated,

summary: A person cannot give as cherem something that is not his. Can Kohanim and Levi'im give things as cherem? The Tannaim argue.

chunks.en: Someone who gives as cherem his son or his daughter,
chunks.st: In the case of one who dedicates his son or his daughter,

chunks.en: his Jewish servant or maidservant,
chunks.st: or his Hebrew slave or maidservant,

chunks.en: or a field that he bought,
chunks.st: or his purchased field,

chunks.en: they are not cherem,
chunks.st: those items are not considered dedicated,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מַחֲרִים דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ.
chunks.en: because a person cannot give as cherem something that is not his.

summary: A person may give his korbanos as cherem; then he gives their value. And how a bechor animal can be made hekdesh for its value but not for the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: A person may give his korbanos as cherem,
chunks.st: As the Sages delineated: A person may dedicate his sacrificial animals,

chunks.he: בֵּין קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים וּבֵין קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים.
chunks.en: both very holy korbanos and lighter korbanos.
chunks.st: both offerings of the most sacred order and offerings of lesser sanctity.

chunks.en: If it was a neder,
chunks.explain: A neder is when he said, "I will bring a korban."
chunks.st: If the offering he dedicated was the object of a vow,
chunks.stMore: e.g., if he said: It is incumbent upon me to sacrifice a burnt offering, since he is obligated to replace such offerings they are considered his property, and therefore

chunks.en: he gives its full value.
chunks.st: he gives their value to the priests.

chunks.en: If it was a nedavah,
chunks.explain: A nedavah is when he said, "This animal is a korban."
chunks.st: And if the offering he dedicated was a gift offering,
chunks.stMore: e.g., if he said: This animal is a burnt offering, in which case he is not obligated to replace the animal,

chunks.en: he gives the value of what he gains from it.
chunks.st: he gives the monetary benefit that he has in them.

chunks.en: "This ox is an olah":
chunks.st: For example, if he said: This bull is a burnt offering,

chunks.en: one pasuk says, "make it holy,"
chunks.st: One verse states: “All the firstborn males that are born of your herd and of your flock you shall consecrate to the Lord your God” (Deuteronomy 15:19),

chunks.en: and one pasuk says, "do not make it holy."
chunks.st: and one verse states: “However, the firstborn among animals that is born first to the Lord, a man shall not consecrate it” (Leviticus 27:26).

chunks.en: We cannot say "make it holy,"
chunks.st: It is impossible to say: “You shall consecrate,”

chunks.en: because it already says "do not make it holy,"
chunks.st: as it is already stated: “A man shall not consecrate.”

chunks.en: and we cannot say "do not make it holy,"
chunks.st: It is likewise impossible to say: “A man shall not consecrate,”

chunks.en: because it already says "make it holy."
chunks.st: as it is already stated: “You shall consecrate.”

chunks.en: So say this:
chunks.st: How, then, can these verses be reconciled?

chunks.en: you can make it hekdesh for its value,
chunks.st: You can consecrate the firstborn animal by a consecration of value,
chunks.stMore: i.e., an individual can donate to the Temple treasury the amount he would be willing to pay for the right to give the firstborn to a specific priest;

chunks.en: but you cannot make it hekdesh for the mizbe'ach.
chunks.st: and you cannot consecrate it by a consecration for the altar, as a firstborn may not be sacrificed for the sake of any other offering.
